**The Weight of a Thousand Words**

The rain fell in sheets, turning the city streets into rivers of silver. I stood under the awning of a closed bookstore, watching the world blur through the downpour. My coat was damp, my shoes soaked, but I didn’t care. I had a thousand words to write, and I wasn’t sure where to begin.

Words had always been my refuge. When the world felt too heavy, I could lose myself in the rhythm of sentences, the dance of metaphors, the quiet hum of meaning. But tonight, the words felt slippery, like fish in my hands—just out of reach.

I thought about the people I’d met today. The old man at the café who spoke in riddles, his eyes crinkled with laughter. The woman on the subway who cried silently, her hands clutching a faded photograph. The child who chased pigeons in the park, his laughter ringing like bells. A thousand stories, a thousand lives, all intersecting in this city that never slept.

I pulled out my notebook, the pages already slightly curled from the humidity. The ink from my pen bled a little as I pressed it to the paper.

*"The city is a living thing,"* I wrote. *"It breathes through the gaps in the pavement, exhales in the steam from subway grates, pulses in the neon signs that flicker like dying stars."*

I paused. Was that enough? A thousand words seemed like a lot, but sometimes the most important things were the ones left unsaid.

I thought about love. Not the grand, sweeping kind from movies, but the quiet, stubborn kind—the kind that lingers in the way someone tucks your hair behind your ear, or the way they remember your favorite coffee order after years apart. I thought about loss, too. The way it sits in your chest like a stone, heavy and unyielding.

*"We are all just trying to be seen,"* I wrote. *"To be understood, even for a moment. To leave a mark, however small, before the world forgets us."*

The rain slowed to a drizzle. The streets glistened, reflecting the glow of streetlights. I closed my notebook, the words inside feeling both too much and not enough.

A thousand words. A thousand thoughts. A thousand fragments of a life that was still unfolding.

I stepped out from under the awning, letting the last of the rain touch my face. The city hummed around me, alive and indifferent.

And I walked on.
